name: Gyvar Payments
author: gyvar

sections.description:
Gyvar Payments puts a Pay button on your WordPress site and adds a payment
gateway to WooCommerce. Your customer pays from a Bitcoin or stablecoin balance;
the money lands in the account you nominate.

What this plugin does:

  • A Pay button block and [gyvar_pay] shortcode, pointing at a payment link
    you created in your Gyvar dashboard. No API key needed.
  • A webhook receiver, so your site is told when a payment completes. Every
    delivery is signature-verified and deduplicated before anything acts on it.
  • A WooCommerce payment gateway. Your customer picks Bitcoin and stablecoins
    at checkout, pays on a page Gyvar hosts, and the order is marked paid by a
    signed webhook – not by the customer coming back, so a closed tab still
    delivers the goods. Works with both the classic and the block checkout.

You need a Gyvar account. The Pay button also needs a payment link from your
Gyvar dashboard; the WooCommerce gateway does not, because it creates a Gyvar
order for each checkout. Fees, corridors and settlement are configured in your
Gyvar dashboard, not here.

External services

This plugin communicates with Gyvar, operated by Gyvar, Inc.

  • The Pay button renders a link to pay.gyvar.com. Nothing is sent from your
    server; your visitor’s browser loads that page when they click.
  • The connection test on the settings screen sends a signed request to
    api.gyvar.com/v1/whoami. It contains your key id, a timestamp, a nonce and a
    signature. It moves no money and returns which key authenticated.
  • The WooCommerce gateway sends a signed request to
    api.gyvar.com/v1/checkout/orders when a customer checks out with Gyvar. It
    contains the order number and total, the currency, your site name and the
    return URLs. It sends no customer name, email or address.
  • The webhook receiver accepts inbound requests from Gyvar at
    /wp-json/gyvar/v1/webhook and verifies their signature. It sends nothing.

No visitor data is transmitted to Gyvar by this plugin. Terms:
https://gyvar.com/legal/terms – Privacy: https://gyvar.com/legal/privacy
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin, then go to Settings > Gyvar Payments.
  2. For webhooks, register the endpoint URL shown on the settings screen in your
    Gyvar dashboard and paste the signing secret it gives you.

For WooCommerce:

  1. Generate a key on the settings screen, upload its public key in your Gyvar
    dashboard with Read and Receive, and paste the key id back.
  2. In your Gyvar dashboard, under Settings > Payment links, add your shop’s
    address as a return address.
  3. Enable Gyvar under WooCommerce > Settings > Payments.

For the Pay button:

  1. Create a payment link in your Gyvar dashboard and paste its slug.
  2. Add the Pay button block to a page, or use [gyvar_pay slug="your-slug"].
sections.faq:
Does uninstalling revoke my API key?

No. Uninstalling deletes the key from this site, but the key stays registered on
Gyvar until you revoke it in your dashboard. Revoke it there first.

Why does the connection test say ip_not_allowed?

The key has an IP allowlist and your server called from another address. The
error message includes the address Gyvar saw; add that one. A store key needs
only read and receive, and those keys do not require an allowlist.

Is the WooCommerce gateway ready?

Yes. It takes live payments on production stores. Use test mode to try it on
your own store before you switch to live.

How do Gyvar statuses map to WooCommerce orders?

  • paid: Processing.
  • paid late (after expiry): Processing, even if already Cancelled. Check stock.
  • expired or cancelled: Cancelled.
  • underpaid and declined: Failed. The money is still in your Gyvar wallet.
  • underpaid, not yet decided: stays On hold. Decide in your Gyvar dashboard.
  • escalated for review: stays On hold until Gyvar resolves it, then follows the
    outcome (paid, or failed if closed or cancelled).
  • superseded by a newer payment: left as it is. Refund the extra in Gyvar.
  • refunded: unchanged. Refund in WooCommerce by hand.

A paid order is never un-paid by a later event.
sections.changelog:
0.1.1

  • BTC, USDT and USDC logos beside the payment method at checkout.
  • The WooCommerce settings screen shows test or live mode, whether a key
    and webhook secret are set, and the setup steps above the settings.

0.1.0

  • First release: Pay button block and shortcode, signature-verified webhook
    receiver, settings screen with key generation and a connection test.
  • WooCommerce gateway for the classic and block checkout, with orders updated
    by signed webhook. Not yet run against a live store.
